laws.title: Indonesian Culture — Right Hand Only; Religious Respect
laws.subtitle: Left hand is unclean; Islam shapes major social norms
laws.fullDescription: Indonesia is the world's largest Muslim-majority country. Always use the right hand for eating, giving, and receiving — the left hand is considered unclean. Remove shoes before entering homes and mosques. During Ramadan, eat and drink discreetly in public. When visiting Bali (Hindu), cover shoulders and hips at temples. Smile and remain calm — losing your temper publicly is deeply shameful.
laws.penalty: Not typically prosecuted — though disrespecting religious sites can result in fines or expulsion.
exceptions: Bali has distinct Hindu customs — different from Islamic Java and Sumatra
Urban Jakarta is more Westernised

quiz.q: What physical gesture is considered unclean and should be avoided in Indonesia?
quiz.explanation: In Indonesia (and much of the Muslim world), the left hand is considered unclean — always use the right hand to give, receive, and eat.

laws.title: Drink Driving — Zero Tolerance Effectively
laws.subtitle: Traffic Law No. 22/2009 — BAC 0.0g/L in practice
laws.fullDescription: Indonesia has near-zero tolerance for alcohol while driving, with a formal limit of 0.0g/L. This is consistent with Islamic law norms. Enforcement at police checkpoints.
laws.penalty: Driving under influence: criminal charges, up to 1 year imprisonment + fine up to Rp 3 million.
exceptions: None

quiz.q: Indonesia's blood alcohol limit for drivers?
quiz.explanation: Indonesia enforces effectively zero tolerance for blood alcohol while driving.

laws.title: Bali Temple Dress Code — Sarong Mandatory
laws.subtitle: Adat law — Entering temple incorrectly is deeply disrespectful
laws.fullDescription: Bali is a Hindu island with strict dress codes at temples (pura). Both men and women must wear a sarong (and often a sash) when entering any Hindu temple. Temples may have menstruation restrictions for women. Tourists who enter temples disrespectfully or behave inappropriately can face expulsion and in extreme cases arrest. Public nudity is illegal nationwide.
laws.penalty: Disrespecting a temple: expulsion + possible arrest under Public Order law. Public nudity: fine up to Rp 4 million or 4 months imprisonment.
exceptions: Hotel pools and designated beach areas for swimwear
Sarongs available to rent/borrow at most temple entrances

quiz.q: What must visitors wear when entering a Balinese Hindu temple?
options: A sarong and sash over their clothing
Long trousers and a collared shirt
quiz.explanation: All visitors to Balinese Hindu temples must wear a sarong and usually a sash — these are typically available to borrow at temple entrances.

laws.title: Drug Laws in Indonesia — Death Penalty for Trafficking
laws.subtitle: Narcotics Law 35/2009 — Extremely strict enforcement
laws.fullDescription: Indonesia has some of the world's strictest drug laws. Drug trafficking can result in the death penalty — multiple Australians were executed in 2015 (Bali Nine). Possession of even small amounts of marijuana can lead to years in prison. Bali and tourist areas are heavily policed. Drug searches at airports are thorough.
laws.penalty: Trafficking: death penalty. Possession (any amount): 4 years minimum to life imprisonment. Using: up to 4 years.
exceptions: None — foreign nationals receive no special treatment

quiz.q: What happened to the Australian 'Bali Nine' drug traffickers in Indonesia?
quiz.explanation: Several members of the Bali Nine were executed by firing squad in 2015 — Indonesia's drug trafficking laws carry the death penalty.

laws.title: Marine and Coral Reef Protection
laws.subtitle: Fisheries Law 45/2009 — Damaging coral is a criminal offence
laws.fullDescription: Indonesia hosts the world's most biodiverse coral reefs as part of the Coral Triangle. Under Fisheries Law No. 45/2009, it is illegal to destroy, damage, or remove coral reef fragments. Tourists who break off coral while snorkelling or diving face heavy fines. Fishing with explosives (blast fishing) or cyanide — common poaching methods — is prohibited and carries imprisonment. Marine protected areas (kawasan konservasi perairan) enforce strict no-take zones around places like Raja Ampat and the Komodo National Park.
laws.penalty: Coral destruction: up to 6 years imprisonment + fines up to IDR 1.5 billion (~USD 95,000); tourist violations: fines starting IDR 2 million
exceptions: Scientific research with government permit
Licensed sustainable fishing in designated zones

quiz.q: What is illegal for divers in Indonesia's marine protected areas?
quiz.explanation: Removing or damaging coral reef fragments is a criminal offence under Indonesian Fisheries Law, with fines up to IDR 1.5 billion.

laws.title: Blasphemy Law (PNPS 1965) — Insulting Religion is a Criminal Offence
laws.subtitle: Presidential Regulation No. 1/PNPS/1965 — Up to 5 years for blasphemy
laws.fullDescription: Indonesia's blasphemy law, rooted in Presidential Regulation No. 1/PNPS/1965, makes it illegal to interpret or carry out religious activities in ways deemed 'deviant' or to insult the six officially recognised religions (Islam, Protestantism, Catholicism, Hinduism, Buddhism, and Confucianism). The law has been used against religious minorities, atheists who publicly declared their non-belief on social media, and LGBT activists. In 2016, the Constitutional Court upheld the law's constitutionality despite human rights concerns. The case of Jakarta Governor Basuki Tjahaja Purnama ('Ahok') in 2017 — sentenced to 2 years for blasphemy during a political campaign — drew international attention to the law's use as a political tool.
laws.penalty: Blasphemy: up to 5 years imprisonment under PNPS 1965. Under the Electronic Information and Transactions (ITE) Law, online religious insults: up to 6 years.
exceptions: Academic theological study and interfaith dialogue in approved institutional contexts
State-recognised religious organisations discussing internal doctrine
laws.sourceLabel: Presidential Regulation No. 1/PNPS/1965 — Blasphemy Law Indonesia

quiz.q: How many religions are officially recognised under Indonesia's blasphemy law?
quiz.explanation: Indonesia officially recognises 6 religions under PNPS 1965 — Islam, Protestantism, Catholicism, Hinduism, Buddhism, and Confucianism. Blasphemy against these carries up to 5 years imprisonment.

laws.title: Volcano Exclusion Zones — Mount Agung, Merapi, Semeru Enforced
laws.subtitle: PVMBG Alert Levels + Regent Decrees — Level III/IV triggers mandatory zone evacuation
laws.fullDescription: Indonesia has about 130 active volcanoes, the most of any nation. The Centre for Volcanology and Geological Hazard Mitigation (PVMBG, part of the Geological Agency) issues a four-level alert system: Normal, Waspada (Alert), Siaga (Standby), Awas (Danger). At Siaga and Awas levels, regional Regents issue decrees establishing exclusion zones — typically 3 km to 8 km radii around active craters. These decrees are legally enforced. Tourists have been fined, deported, and in some cases prosecuted for breaching zones at Mount Agung (Bali), Mount Bromo, Mount Merapi, Mount Semeru, Mount Rinjani and Mount Sinabung. Following the 2021 Mount Semeru eruption, which killed 51 people, and the 2023 Marapi (West Sumatra) eruption which killed 23 hikers who ignored warnings, enforcement has intensified. Hiking permits for volcanoes are revoked whenever alert level rises to Siaga.
laws.penalty: Entering an exclusion zone: fines up to Rp 50 million + deportation for foreigners. Gross negligence causing rescuer injury or death: up to 5 years imprisonment under the Indonesian Criminal Code. Hiking guides operating in prohibited zones: licence revocation.
exceptions: Authorised PVMBG researchers and SAR teams under command
Community evacuation support operations coordinated by the local regent
laws.sourceLabel: PVMBG Volcano Alert System — Geological Agency of Indonesia

quiz.q: At which PVMBG alert level are volcano exclusion zones typically imposed by Regent decree in Indonesia?
options: Only when the volcano has already erupted
quiz.explanation: PVMBG’s 4-level system triggers mandatory Regent-issued exclusion zones (3–8 km) at Siaga (Standby) and Awas (Danger). Hiking permits are revoked and violators face fines and deportation.

laws.title: Bali Hindu Temples — Strict Dress Codes; Menstruating Women Barred Entry
laws.subtitle: Awig-Awig customary law — Sarong required; menstrual exclusion enforced
laws.fullDescription: Bali's Hindu temples (pura) operate under Awig-Awig — traditional Balinese customary law that governs temple access. All visitors must wear a sarong and sash (provided at the entrance for a small fee); shoulders must be covered. Women who are menstruating are traditionally barred from entering temples — signs at major temples like Tanah Lot and Besakih explicitly state this. This rule is an ancient Hindu purification belief and is strictly observed by local communities. Certain high-caste (Brahmin) ceremonies are closed entirely to non-Hindus. Photography of odalan (temple anniversary ceremonies) requires explicit permission from the priest (pemangku). Entering a temple during an active ceremony without invitation is considered a serious offence.
laws.penalty: Entering a temple without a sarong: immediate refusal of entry. Photographing ceremonies without permission: camera confiscation by temple committee.
exceptions: Invited guests of Balinese families during ceremonies
Accredited cultural researchers with PHDI (Hindu Council of Indonesia) permission

quiz.q: What traditional Balinese customary legal system governs temple rules and community conduct in Bali?
quiz.explanation: Awig-Awig is Bali's traditional customary law system governing village and temple conduct — it operates alongside Indonesian national law and regulates everything from temple access to community responsibilities and environmental rules.

laws.title: ITE Law (Electronic Information and Transactions) — Broad Online Speech Restrictions
laws.subtitle: Indonesia's 'rubber article' defamation law used against government critics and private disputes
laws.fullDescription: Indonesia's Law No. 11 of 2008 on Electronic Information and Transactions (ITE Law), especially Article 27 (defamation) and Article 28 (hate speech/fake news), has been used extensively to prosecute online speech. Critics call it the 'rubber article' because its vague wording stretches to cover almost any online statement. Activists, journalists, domestic abuse victims (for posting about abusers), and even disaster victims warning about dangerous conditions have been prosecuted. President Joko Widodo promised revisions after public backlash; the 2022 amendment narrowed some provisions but left core issues intact. The law applies to all online content including private messages, social media, and group chats. Maximum sentence: 6 years imprisonment + fines.
laws.penalty: Online defamation (Article 27): up to 4 years imprisonment + fines up to IDR 750 million (~$48,000). Distributing false news (Article 28): up to 6 years + IDR 1 billion (~$64,000) fines.
exceptions: Journalistic content by licensed press organizations under Press Law
Official government communications
Academic publications in registered journals
laws.sourceLabel: Indonesian Ministry of Communications — ITE Law

quiz.q: Why is Indonesia's ITE Law called the 'rubber article' law?
options: It was drafted by the rubber industry lobby
Its vague wording stretches to cover almost any online statement
It requires rubber-stamped approvals from authorities
It can be stretched to apply in any court jurisdiction
quiz.explanation: Indonesia's ITE Law is called the 'rubber article' because its vague defamation and hate speech provisions can be 'stretched' to prosecute a wide range of online speech — from activists criticizing the government to domestic abuse victims posting about their abusers.

laws.title: Orangutan Poaching and Habitat Protection — Indonesia's Endangered Primate Laws
laws.subtitle: All three orangutan species are critically endangered; habitat destruction is the primary threat
laws.fullDescription: Indonesia hosts three orangutan species (Bornean, Sumatran, and newly described Tapanuli) — all Critically Endangered under IUCN Red List. Indonesia's Law No. 5 of 1990 on Conservation of Natural Resources and Ecosystems (UUCB) protects orangutans as fully protected species: killing, capturing, possessing, or trading them is illegal. Penalties are severe but enforcement is challenging in remote forest areas. The primary threat is habitat loss — palm oil plantations and paper pulp plantations have destroyed 80% of Borneo's lowland forests over 30 years. The Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) certifies deforestation-free palm oil but certification gaps exist. Borneo fires (deliberately set to clear land) regularly kill hundreds of orangutans. BOSF (Borneo Orangutan Survival Foundation) operates the world's largest orangutan rehabilitation center.
laws.penalty: Killing an orangutan: up to 5 years imprisonment + fines up to IDR 100 million (~$6,400). Possessing or trading: same penalties. Deliberately setting fires destroying habitat: up to 15 years imprisonment.
exceptions: Orangutan welfare research by LIPI-authorized institutions
Emergency rescue of orangutans by BKSDA conservation officers
Rehabilitation and reintroduction programs by licensed NGOs
laws.sourceLabel: Borneo Orangutan Survival Foundation — Conservation Status

quiz.q: How many orangutan species exist in Indonesia, and what is their conservation status?
quiz.explanation: Indonesia has three orangutan species: Bornean (Pongo pygmaeus), Sumatran (Pongo abelii), and the recently described Tapanuli (Pongo tapanuliensis) — all three are classified as Critically Endangered on the IUCN Red List, primarily due to habitat destruction from palm oil and paper pulp plantation expansion.

laws.title: Indonesian New Criminal Code — Sex Outside Marriage Criminalized; Press Freedom Concerns
laws.subtitle: Indonesia passed a new criminal code in 2022; cohabitation and sex outside marriage become criminal
laws.fullDescription: Indonesia's new Criminal Code (KUHP Baru), passed December 2022 and effective January 2026, replaces the Dutch colonial-era penal code. Controversial provisions: sex outside marriage is criminalized with up to 1 year imprisonment (prosecuted only on complaint by a close relative or spouse — 'adulterer complaint'). Cohabitation by unmarried couples: up to 6 months imprisonment (complaint-based). Insulting the president: up to 3 years. Attacking 'state dignity': up to 5 years. Spreading communism: up to 4 years. International concern focused on sex-related provisions applying to foreign tourists. Indonesia's government argued family members would rarely file complaints and the law codifies existing Sharia-influenced local regulations nationally. LGBTQ+ advocates noted no explicit criminalization of homosexuality at national level (some provincial regulations do).
laws.penalty: Sex outside marriage (complaint filed): up to 1 year imprisonment. Cohabitation (complaint filed): up to 6 months. Insulting president: up to 3 years. Spreading communism: up to 4 years.
exceptions: Prosecution for sex/cohabitation requires complaint from family member — state cannot initiate prosecution
Foreign nationals in recognized civil unions under their home country law may have some protections
Married couples are fully exempt from sex-related provisions
laws.sourceLabel: Indonesian Ministry of Law — New Criminal Code KUHP

quiz.q: Who can trigger prosecution under Indonesia's new criminal code provision criminalizing sex outside marriage?
options: Only a close relative or spouse of the parties involved
quiz.explanation: Indonesia's new criminal code provision criminalizing sex outside marriage can only be triggered by a complaint from a close relative or spouse of the parties involved — the state cannot initiate prosecution on its own. This complaint-based structure was intended to limit prosecution to genuine family disputes, though international observers still raised concerns about tourist exposure to the law.

laws.title: Nusantara New Capital Project
laws.subtitle: Indonesia is relocating its capital from sinking Jakarta to a new city carved from Borneo jungle
laws.fullDescription: In January 2022, Indonesia's parliament approved moving the national capital from Jakarta — which is sinking up to 25cm per year due to groundwater extraction, increasingly flooded, and overwhelmed with 30 million people — to a new city called Nusantara on the island of Borneo (Kalimantan). The project, estimated at $33 billion, involves clearing jungle, building government buildings, and eventually relocating 1.5 million civil servants. Indigenous Dayak communities raised land rights concerns. Environmental groups warned of deforestation. The first government buildings were inaugurated in 2024. Critics questioned the cost during an economic slowdown.
laws.penalty: Illegal logging or land clearing in the Nusantara development zone without permits: 5–15 years imprisonment. Indigenous communities' customary land rights must be addressed through formal recognition processes.
exceptions: Jakarta remains Indonesia's economic and financial center regardless of capital relocation
Indigenous community land rights are formally recognized under the Constitutional Court's 2013 ruling
Environmental impact assessments are legally required for each development phase

quiz.q: Why is Indonesia moving its capital from Jakarta to the new city of Nusantara?
options: Jakarta was destroyed by an earthquake
Jakarta is sinking up to 25cm per year due to groundwater extraction and faces chronic flooding
Jakarta is too cold for the government to function
The population voted in a referendum for a new capital
quiz.explanation: Jakarta is sinking up to 25 centimeters per year due to excessive groundwater extraction, is regularly flooded, and is overwhelmed with 30 million people — making the decision to build a new capital, Nusantara, on Borneo both an environmental and urban planning necessity.

laws.title: Prabowo Presidency — Former General Elected
laws.subtitle: Prabowo Subianto, accused of human rights abuses in East Timor, became Indonesia's 8th president in 2024
laws.fullDescription: Prabowo Subianto won Indonesia's February 2024 presidential election with 58.6% of the vote — his third attempt after losses in 2014 and 2019. Prabowo is a former special forces general who was dismissed from the military in 1998 for alleged human rights abuses in East Timor (now Timor-Leste) during the independence crisis. He was denied a US visa multiple times over these allegations. His political rehabilitation — including serving as Defense Minister under Jokowi — and his choice of Jokowi's son Gibran Rakabuming as running mate (requiring a controversial Constitutional Court age exception) reflected Indonesia's complex politics. Prabowo took office October 20, 2024.
laws.penalty: Past human rights violations: Indonesia's accountability mechanisms remain weak — no prosecutions for Timor-Leste abuses. Election-related disputes: Constitutional Court review. The Constitutional Court ruling allowing Gibran's candidacy at age 36 triggered ethics complaints against the Chief Justice.
exceptions: The statute of limitations and political accommodation limit historical accountability
Indonesia's National Human Rights Commission (Komnas HAM) reports on past abuses without binding enforcement
Timor-Leste itself has pursued reconciliation rather than prosecution

quiz.q: What controversy surrounded Prabowo's choice of Jokowi's son Gibran as running mate?
options: Gibran was not an Indonesian citizen
A Constitutional Court ruling created a special age exception enabling Gibran to run at 36
quiz.explanation: Gibran Rakabuming was below the minimum age for vice presidential candidates, but a controversial Constitutional Court ruling created an exception for candidates with local government experience — with the Chief Justice being Jokowi's brother-in-law — enabling Gibran to run.

laws.title: Blasphemy Law: Criminal Defamation of Religion
laws.subtitle: Indonesia's 1965 blasphemy law has increasingly been used to jail minority religious practitioners and atheists
laws.fullDescription: Indonesia's Law No. 1/PNPS/1965 on Blasphemy criminalizes the distortion or misinterpretation of the six officially recognized religions (Islam, Protestantism, Catholicism, Hinduism, Buddhism, and Confucianism). The law carries up to 5 years imprisonment. Its application has intensified in the 2010s–2020s: Jakarta's Christian governor Basuki 'Ahok' Tjahaja Purnama was convicted in 2017 after Islamic hardliners accused him of blasphemy for quoting a Quran verse. Atheists have been jailed for posting about their non-belief on social media. Ahmadiyya Muslims face violent persecution since a 2008 decree labeled their beliefs deviant.
laws.penalty: Up to 5 years imprisonment for blasphemy. Forcible dissolution of organizations deemed to distort religion
exceptions: Religious criticism in clearly academic or research contexts receives more lenient treatment
The six recognized religions themselves cannot be prosecuted for internal theological disagreements
laws.sourceLabel: Human Rights Watch – Indonesia Religious Freedom

quiz.q: How many religions are officially recognized by Indonesia's blasphemy law?
quiz.explanation: Indonesia officially recognizes six religions under its blasphemy law: Islam, Protestantism, Catholicism, Hinduism, Buddhism, and Confucianism. Practitioners of other beliefs — including Ahmadiyya Muslims and atheists — face prosecution.

laws.title: Nusantara: Indonesia Moves Its Capital from Sinking Jakarta
laws.subtitle: Indonesia passed a law to move its capital to Borneo — as Jakarta sinks 25cm per year and faces catastrophic flooding
laws.fullDescription: Jakarta, home to 30 million people, is one of the world's fastest-sinking cities: parts of North Jakarta have sunk 2.5 meters in the past decade due to excessive groundwater extraction, and 40% of the city is below sea level. In January 2022, Indonesia's parliament passed the Nusantara Capital City Law, officially moving the national capital to a new city called Nusantara in East Kalimantan (Borneo). The total cost is estimated at $35 billion. The first government offices began moving in 2024. Critics raised concerns about deforestation (the site is in tropical rainforest), Indigenous Dayak land rights, and the enormous expense while millions of Indonesians live in poverty. President Prabowo (who took office in 2024) signaled continued support for the project.
laws.penalty: No criminal penalties for citizens — this is a capital city relocation project. Land acquisition for Nusantara follows Indonesia's Land Acquisition Law (2012)
exceptions: Jakarta retains status as a 'Special Region' and economic capital even after governmental functions move
Certain national institutions may remain in Jakarta under transitional arrangements

quiz.q: By how much do parts of North Jakarta sink each year, driving the capital relocation decision?
quiz.explanation: Parts of North Jakarta sink approximately 25cm (about 10 inches) per year due to massive groundwater extraction — meaning some areas have sunk 2.5 meters in a decade. Combined with 40% of the city being below sea level, this made Jakarta's long-term habitability as a capital untenable.

laws.title: Blasphemy Law
laws.subtitle: Indonesia's blasphemy law carries up to 5 years imprisonment
laws.fullDescription: Indonesia's Law No. 1/PNPS/1965 on the Prevention of Blasphemy, upheld by the Constitutional Court in 2010, prohibits insults, deviations, or misinterpretations of the six state-recognized religions: Islam, Protestantism, Catholicism, Hinduism, Buddhism, and Confucianism. Violations carry up to 5 years imprisonment. The law has been used against members of minority religious groups, atheists who express their views publicly, and minority Muslim sects like Ahmadiyya. In 2016, Jakarta's Christian governor Basuki Tjahaja Purnama ('Ahok') was convicted of blasphemy after political opponents accused him of insulting the Quran during a speech.
laws.penalty: Up to 5 years imprisonment; organizations can be banned for promoting blasphemous teachings
exceptions: Academic discussion within recognized religious institutions is generally permitted
Religious criticism in private is rarely prosecuted

quiz.q: Which Jakarta governor was convicted of blasphemy in 2016?
quiz.explanation: Basuki Tjahaja Purnama, known as 'Ahok', was Jakarta's Christian governor convicted of blasphemy in 2017 after political opponents used a speech about Quran interpretation to fuel mass protests against him.

laws.title: Palm Oil Moratorium
laws.subtitle: Indonesia's presidential moratorium paused new palm oil plantation licenses
laws.fullDescription: Indonesia's Presidential Instruction No. 8/2018 imposed a three-year moratorium on new palm oil plantation licenses, extended in 2021, covering approximately 16 million hectares. Indonesia and Malaysia together produce over 85% of the world's palm oil. Indonesian law mandates that all palm oil exports be certified sustainable under the Indonesian Sustainable Palm Oil (ISPO) standard. Despite the moratorium, deforestation linked to palm oil expansion has continued through existing permits and illegal clearing. The EU's Deforestation Regulation (2023) requiring imported palm oil to be deforestation-free has significant implications for Indonesia's palm oil industry.
laws.penalty: Clearing forest for palm oil without permits: criminal prosecution under Forestry Law — up to 15 years; plantation operations without ISPO certification: export bans
exceptions: Existing plantations with valid licenses are not affected by the moratorium
Smallholder farmers (under 25 hectares) have simplified ISPO certification requirements
laws.sourceLabel: Indonesian Ministry of Environment and Forestry

quiz.q: What share of the world's palm oil do Indonesia and Malaysia together produce?
quiz.explanation: Indonesia and Malaysia together produce over 85% of the world's palm oil — the most widely used vegetable oil globally, found in approximately half of all supermarket products including food, cosmetics, and biofuels.

laws.title: New Capital City Law
laws.subtitle: Indonesia passed a law to move its capital from Jakarta to Nusantara in Borneo
laws.fullDescription: Indonesia's Capital City Law (IKN Law, 2022) authorized the creation of Nusantara — a new capital city in East Kalimantan (Borneo) — to replace Jakarta, which faces flooding, sinking land (40% below sea level), extreme congestion, and pollution. President Jokowi made the move a legacy project; groundbreaking occurred in 2022. The new capital is designed for 1.9 million civil servants and government workers. Construction began but faced significant delays, funding shortfalls, and a legal challenge from indigenous Dayak communities. By 2024, some government functions had moved to Nusantara, but full relocation is not expected until 2045.
laws.penalty: Unauthorized development within the IKN Authority zone: demolition orders; indigenous land violations: subject to ongoing court challenges
exceptions: Jakarta will remain the business and economic capital — only government functions move
Existing indigenous community settlements have protected rights under the IKN Law

quiz.q: In which Indonesian island is the new capital Nusantara being built?
quiz.explanation: Nusantara, Indonesia's new capital, is being built in East Kalimantan on the island of Borneo — chosen for its central geographic location, lower earthquake risk than Java, and availability of land away from Jakarta's overcrowded, sinking, and flood-prone areas.

laws.title: New Criminal Code 2023 (KUHP Baru)
laws.subtitle: Indonesia's 2023 criminal code overhaul includes controversial provisions on cohabitation and insulting the president
laws.fullDescription: Indonesia's parliament passed a comprehensive new Criminal Code (Kitab Undang-Undang Hukum Pidana/KUHP) in December 2022, replacing the Dutch colonial-era code from 1918. The code took effect on January 2, 2026 (after a transition period). Major changes include: criminalization of cohabitation outside marriage (up to 6 months imprisonment, but only if filed by a parent, spouse, or village head — not police); insult to the president or state institutions (up to 3 years); criminalizing 'promoting contraceptives' without authorization (in contexts deemed to encourage promiscuity); and expanding blasphemy provisions. International business groups, human rights organizations, and women's rights advocates raised significant concerns. The cohabitation provision could affect millions of unmarried couples and foreign workers. Indonesia's legal system blends Dutch civil law, Islamic law (in family matters), customary adat law, and national legislation.
laws.penalty: Cohabitation outside marriage: up to 6 months imprisonment; presidential insult: up to 3 years; blasphemy: up to 5 years (existing provision incorporated)
exceptions: Cohabitation offenses are 'aduan' (complaint-driven) — police cannot proactively enforce, only act on family complaints
Medical professionals prescribing contraceptives are exempt
Legal marriage recognized under any of Indonesia's recognized religions is fully exempt

laws.title: Nusantara New Capital City Law
laws.subtitle: Indonesia's decision to build a new capital on Borneo moved the seat of government from Jakarta
laws.fullDescription: Indonesia enacted Law No. 3/2022 on the State Capital (Ibu Kota Negara/IKN), establishing Nusantara as the new national capital on the island of Borneo (East Kalimantan province). President Joko Widodo signed the law in January 2022 after announcing the capital relocation in 2019. The move is driven by: Jakarta's extreme overcrowding (12+ million people, one of the world's largest cities); the city sinking (parts of North Jakarta have sunk 4 meters and could be fully submerged by 2050); pollution; and a desire to shift development to the island of Borneo and outside Java. Nusantara is planned to eventually house 1.9 million people on a 256,142 hectare site. The IKN Law created the Nusantara Capital City Authority (OIKN) as an independent body with special governance powers. Construction has proceeded but faced funding challenges and land rights disputes with indigenous Dayak communities who live in the designated area.
laws.penalty: Encroachment on IKN development areas after zoning: fines and eviction; violations of environmental management plan for IKN: regulatory sanctions; unauthorized construction: demolition orders
exceptions: Indigenous Dayak communities are theoretically protected under indigenous rights provisions
FPIC consultation is required under Indonesian environmental law
Areas outside the IKN core zone retain normal land use governance

laws.title: Prabowo Subianto Elected President – Defense and Democracy
laws.subtitle: Indonesia elected a former general with human rights controversies as president
laws.fullDescription: In February 2024, Prabowo Subianto — a former military general and son-in-law of former dictator Suharto — won Indonesia's presidential election with 58.6% of the vote. His running mate was Gibran Rakabuming Raka, President Joko Widodo's son — a Constitutional Court ruling lowered the minimum age requirement to allow Gibran's candidacy, a decision widely criticized as politically motivated (the court chief at the time was Jokowi's brother-in-law). Prabowo was banned from entering the US for years due to alleged human rights abuses in East Timor in 1998. Human rights groups raised concerns, but Prabowo won on economic promises and Jokowi's implicit support. He took office in October 2024.
laws.penalty: Defense procurement corruption: up to 20 years imprisonment under KPK (anti-corruption) authority. Violation of civil liberties during operations: military tribunal or civil court jurisdiction depending on actor.
exceptions: Presidential immunity for official actions — civil suits challenging presidential decisions face procedural barriers
Constitutional Court decisions binding regardless of political criticism

quiz.q: What constitutional controversy surrounded Prabowo's running mate Gibran Rakabuming Raka?
options: Gibran held dual citizenship which the constitution prohibits
A Constitutional Court ruling lowered the minimum age requirement to allow Gibran's candidacy
Gibran had never held elected office, violating a prior-service requirement
He refused to disclose his financial assets as required
quiz.explanation: The Constitutional Court lowered the minimum age for presidential candidates from 40 to 35, allowing Gibran (Jokowi's son) to run — the ruling was widely criticized as the court chief was Jokowi's brother-in-law.

laws.title: Papua's Special Autonomy Revision and Ongoing Conflict
laws.subtitle: Indonesia revised Papua's autonomy law while armed conflict with independence groups intensified
laws.fullDescription: Indonesia's Papua province (and the newer Papua Pegunungan, Papua Selatan, Papua Tengah provinces created by 2022 division) has been under Special Autonomy since 2001, giving the region additional resources and requiring a Papuan governor. The Special Autonomy Law was revised in 2021 for a 20-year extension (until 2041), increasing the Special Autonomy Fund significantly. However, armed conflict with the West Papua National Liberation Army (TPNPB — OPM's armed wing) has intensified. Hostage-taking of workers and missionaries, killings of military personnel, and retaliatory operations have occurred regularly. Indonesia restricts foreign journalist access to Papua, making independent reporting difficult.
laws.penalty: Armed rebellion in Papua: criminal prosecution under terrorism and treason laws. Advocating Papuan independence: up to 20 years imprisonment.
exceptions: Special Autonomy gives Papua additional political representation rights
Humanitarian organizations have limited access under negotiated agreements

quiz.q: What did Indonesia do to Papua's administrative structure in 2022 alongside the Special Autonomy extension?
options: It unified all Papua provinces into a single administrative region
It divided Papua into four new provinces, diluting the original autonomy arrangement
It granted Papua full control over its mining revenues
It established a joint Indonesia-Papua legislative council
quiz.explanation: In 2022, Indonesia divided Papua into four provinces (Papua, Papua Pegunungan, Papua Selatan, Papua Tengah), which critics — including Papuan independence advocates — argued diluted the original Special Autonomy by splitting the region and its resources.

laws.title: Indonesia's ITE Law and Digital Speech Restrictions
laws.subtitle: Electronic Information and Transactions Law criminalizes online defamation
laws.fullDescription: Indonesia's Law on Electronic Information and Transactions (ITE Law, 2008, revised 2016 and 2024) criminalizes distributing electronic content deemed defamatory, indecent, or related to gambling or blackmail. Article 27 on defamation has been widely used to prosecute government critics, journalists, and ordinary citizens for social media posts. The 2024 revision attempted to narrow the defamation provisions but controversially added provisions on 'false information' affecting public order. Indonesia also requires registration of electronic system operators.
laws.penalty: Electronic defamation: up to 4 years imprisonment or IDR 750 million fine (~$47,000). Distributing indecent content: up to 6 years and IDR 1 billion fine. Impersonation online: up to 12 years and IDR 12 billion fine
exceptions: Journalism by registered press institutions has some protection
Academic and scientific commentary may be protected
Satire that is clearly labeled may have defenses in some courts
laws.sourceLabel: Indonesian Ministry of Communication and Informatics

quiz.q: What has Indonesia's ITE Law Article 27 on defamation been widely criticized for?
options: Being used to prosecute government critics and journalists for social media posts
Allowing foreign companies to avoid Indonesian law
quiz.explanation: Indonesia's ITE Law Article 27 on electronic defamation has been widely criticized for being used by powerful individuals and government officials to prosecute critics, journalists, and ordinary citizens for social media posts.

laws.title: Indonesia's New Capital Nusantara and Land Law
laws.subtitle: Moving the capital from Java to Borneo triggers land acquisition challenges
laws.fullDescription: Indonesia is constructing Nusantara, a new capital city in East Kalimantan (Borneo), to replace Jakarta — which faces severe flooding, land subsidence, and overcrowding. The Nusantara Capital Authority Law (2022) established the governance framework. Land acquisition for the city required displacing indigenous Dayak communities and forest communities, triggering protests and legal challenges about free, prior, and informed consent. President Jokowi moved his office there in 2024. The project has faced funding shortfalls with many private investors pulling back, and the timeline for full government relocation has slipped.
laws.penalty: Land occupation without permit in Nusantara zone: eviction and fines. Unauthorized construction: demolition orders. Illegal deforestation in Kalimantan for capital area: up to 10 years and fines. Obstructing authorized land acquisition: up to 4 years imprisonment
exceptions: Indigenous communities have constitutional adat (customary law) land rights recognized in principle
Land acquisition compensation is mandatory but disputed on adequacy
Environmental impact assessment challenges can delay but not permanently block acquisition

quiz.q: Why is Indonesia building Nusantara as a new capital city?
options: Jakarta is landlocked and lacks a port
Jakarta faces severe flooding, land subsidence, and overcrowding
The government wanted a more central location
Jakarta was damaged in a major earthquake
quiz.explanation: Jakarta faces severe environmental challenges including land subsidence (sinking up to 25 cm per year in some areas), regular flooding, extreme traffic congestion, and overpopulation — driving Indonesia's plan to relocate the capital to Nusantara in Borneo.

laws.title: Indonesia's Nickel Export Ban and EV Battery Push
laws.subtitle: Indonesia bans raw nickel exports to force value-added processing domestically
laws.fullDescription: Indonesia imposed a ban on raw nickel ore exports in 2020 and has maintained it despite losing a WTO case brought by the EU. Indonesia holds 40% of the world's nickel reserves — critical for electric vehicle batteries. The export ban forces foreign companies to build processing facilities in Indonesia to access the ore. This 'downstreaming' policy has attracted Chinese, Korean, and US battery companies to invest in Indonesian processing capacity. Indonesia aims to become a major battery supply chain hub. The WTO ruled the ban violated trade rules, but Indonesia appeals and maintained the ban, citing industrial policy necessity.
laws.penalty: Exporting raw nickel ore without processing: criminal prosecution plus confiscation. Operating smelter without Indonesian environmental permits: closure and fines. Labor violations in nickel processing: fines up to IDR 5 billion. Environmental damage to nickel mining areas: criminal prosecution
exceptions: Low-grade nickel ore (below threshold) may have different treatment
Joint ventures with Indonesian state companies have accelerated permitting
Nickel for scientific research can be exported in limited quantities
laws.sourceLabel: Indonesian Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources

quiz.q: How did Indonesia respond to losing a WTO case about its nickel export ban?
options: Immediately lifted the ban as required
Paid WTO-mandated compensation but kept the ban
Appealed and maintained the ban, citing industrial policy necessity
quiz.explanation: When the WTO ruled Indonesia's nickel export ban violated trade rules in a case brought by the EU, Indonesia appealed and maintained the ban anyway — prioritizing its industrial policy goal of building domestic battery processing capacity over WTO compliance.

laws.title: ITE Law and Criminal Defamation Online
laws.subtitle: Indonesia's Electronic Information and Transactions Law criminalizes online defamation
laws.fullDescription: Indonesia's Law on Electronic Information and Transactions (ITE Law, Law No. 11/2008) criminalized a wide range of online conduct including defamation, spreading false information, and distributing content deemed offensive. The law was amended in 2016 and revised again in 2024 to address criticism that its defamation provisions were vague and abused. High-profile cases included ordinary citizens jailed for WhatsApp messages complaining about local officials. The Constitutional Court limited some applications, but criminal defamation online remains enforceable. Social media users should be extremely careful about critical posts targeting individuals, companies, or officials in Indonesia.
laws.penalty: Online defamation under ITE: up to 4 years imprisonment and fines; spreading false information causing public unrest: up to 6 years
exceptions: Legitimate journalistic work following press ethics guidelines
Official government communications

quiz.q: What common online activity has led to criminal prosecution under Indonesia's ITE Law?
quiz.explanation: Indonesia's ITE Law has been used to criminally prosecute ordinary citizens for WhatsApp messages and social media posts that were deemed defamatory toward local officials or businesses.

laws.title: New Criminal Code and Cohabitation Criminalization
laws.subtitle: Indonesia's new criminal code criminalizes extramarital sex and cohabitation
laws.fullDescription: Indonesia's new Criminal Code (KUHP), passed in 2022 and taking effect in 2026, includes provisions criminalizing consensual sex outside marriage and cohabitation by unmarried couples. These provisions apply to all people in Indonesia including foreigners, though prosecution requires a complaint from family members or limited other parties. Critics warned the law would harm tourism and investment and violate human rights. The code also criminalizes attacks on presidential dignity and restricts abortion more tightly. Some provisions were softened in revisions, and implementation details were debated. The law represents a significant social conservatism shift in Indonesia's legal system.
laws.penalty: Extramarital sex: up to 1 year imprisonment; cohabitation: up to 6 months; insulting the president: up to 3 years
exceptions: Prosecution requires complaint from spouse, parents, or children (not police initiative)
Married couples obviously exempt from extramarital sex provisions
laws.sourceLabel: Indonesia Ministry of Law and Human Rights

quiz.q: Who must file a complaint for Indonesia's new criminal code provisions on extramarital sex to be prosecuted?
options: Only family members (spouse, parents, or children)
quiz.explanation: Indonesia's new criminal code provisions on extramarital sex require a complaint from specific family members (spouse, parents, or children) before prosecution can proceed — they are not public order offenses that police can prosecute independently.

laws.title: Prabowo Election and Dynastic Politics Legal Questions
laws.subtitle: Indonesia's 2024 election victory of Prabowo raised constitutional questions about dynasticism
laws.fullDescription: Prabowo Subianto won Indonesia's February 2024 presidential election with 58% of the vote, with Jokowi's son Gibran Rakabuming Raka as his running mate. Gibran's candidacy required the Constitutional Court (led by Jokowi's brother-in-law) to lower the age threshold for vice-presidential candidates — a decision widely criticized as enabling political dynasticism. The ruling sparked protests and questions about judicial independence. Prabowo's government then proceeded to appoint large numbers of cabinet members and advisors, expanding government size. Indonesia's Constitution limits presidential terms to two, but the dynastic succession raised concerns about formal and informal power concentration.
laws.penalty: Electoral law violations: prosecution before Bawaslu (election supervisory body); constitutional challenges to candidacy rules: Constitutional Court review
exceptions: Normal political activities and campaign finance within legal limits
Opposition party activities fully protected under democratic framework

quiz.q: What did Indonesia's Constitutional Court change to allow Gibran Rakabuming Raka's candidacy?
options: The age threshold for vice-presidential candidates
quiz.explanation: Indonesia's Constitutional Court lowered the age threshold for vice-presidential candidates to allow Gibran Rakabuming Raka (Jokowi's son) to run — a decision criticized as judicially enabling political dynasticism when the court was led by Jokowi's brother-in-law.

laws.title: Indonesia Personal Data Protection Law
laws.subtitle: Indonesia enacts comprehensive data protection with 2-year transition
laws.fullDescription: Indonesia's Personal Data Protection Law (UU PDP) was passed in October 2022 and provides a two-year transition period for compliance. The law establishes rights for data subjects including access, correction, deletion, and objection to processing. Data controllers must have a legal basis for processing, implement security measures, and notify authorities of data breaches within 14 days. Indonesia also established a national data protection supervisory body under the Ministry of Communication.
laws.penalty: Criminal penalties including up to 6 years imprisonment for deliberate misuse of data; administrative fines up to 2% of annual revenue
exceptions: National defense and security
Law enforcement activities
Statistical purposes by government agencies

quiz.q: How long did Indonesia give businesses to comply after passing the Personal Data Protection Law?
quiz.explanation: Indonesia's UU PDP provided a two-year transition period from its October 2022 passage for businesses to come into compliance with the new data protection requirements.

laws.title: Indonesia New Capital City Laws — Nusantara
laws.subtitle: Indonesia enacts laws relocating the capital from Jakarta to Borneo
laws.fullDescription: Indonesia enacted the Capital City Law in 2022 establishing Nusantara as the new capital, located in East Kalimantan (Borneo). The law creates a special governance structure for the new capital city, exempting it from standard regional autonomy rules and placing it under direct central government authority. Development of Nusantara has proceeded in phases, with some government ministries beginning operations there in 2024. The move aims to relieve pressure on sinking, congested Jakarta and shift development focus to eastern Indonesia.
laws.penalty: Violations of Nusantara special zone regulations carry administrative penalties; land disputes in the development zone may involve criminal trespass
exceptions: Existing residents of the development area retain rights during transition
Traditional indigenous land claims being adjudicated separately
Existing business licenses in the zone honored during transition

quiz.q: Why did Indonesia decide to move its capital from Jakarta to Nusantara in Borneo?
options: To relieve pressure on sinking, congested Jakarta and shift development to eastern Indonesia
Jakarta was destroyed in an earthquake
quiz.explanation: Indonesia decided to relocate its capital to relieve pressure on Jakarta, which faces subsidence (the city is literally sinking), severe traffic congestion, flooding, and overdevelopment, while also diversifying development toward eastern Indonesia.

laws.title: Indonesia New Criminal Code — Colonial Law Replaced
laws.subtitle: Indonesia replaces Dutch colonial criminal code with nationalist legislation
laws.fullDescription: Indonesia's new Criminal Code (KUHP), enacted in 2022 and taking effect in 2026 after a 3-year transition, replaces the Dutch colonial penal code of 1918. The code includes controversial provisions including: criminalization of insulting the president, criminalization of cohabitation by unmarried couples (with limited enforcement provisions), extramarital sex offenses, and restrictions on distributing contraception information. Human rights groups and foreign governments raised concerns about impacts on personal freedom and press.
laws.penalty: Insulting the president: up to 3 years; cohabitation by unmarried couple: up to 1 year (with complaint requirement limiting enforcement); extramarital sex: up to 1 year
exceptions: Reports to police only; the cohabitation and sex offenses require complaint from spouse or close family
Foreign tourists have raised concerns — government clarified enforcement not targeted at tourists
Religious minorities retain rights to marry under their own religious laws

quiz.q: What did Indonesia's new Criminal Code replace?
options: A Dutch colonial penal code from 1918
quiz.explanation: Indonesia's new Criminal Code replaced the Dutch colonial penal code of 1918 — over a century old — though its controversial personal morality provisions attracted international concern upon enactment.

laws.title: Job Creation Law (Omnibus Law)
laws.subtitle: Indonesia's sweeping economic and labor deregulation
laws.fullDescription: Indonesia's Job Creation Law (Cipta Kerja) was a landmark omnibus reform amending over 70 existing laws to simplify business licensing, reform labor regulations, ease environmental permit requirements, and attract foreign investment. For workers, it changed severance pay calculations, introduced a new government-funded unemployment benefit, relaxed restrictions on fixed-term contracts, and simplified outsourcing rules. Environmental impact assessments were replaced with risk-based compliance. The law faced significant protests and was twice revised after Constitutional Court challenges.
laws.penalty: Labor violations under the reformed framework carry graduated fines; operating businesses without proper risk-based permits carries administrative and potential criminal liability
exceptions: Micro and small enterprises benefit from simplified licensing and reduced obligations
Strategic national projects have expedited permit pathways
Traditional and indigenous community activities have protected status

quiz.q: How many existing laws did Indonesia's Job Creation omnibus law amend in one legislative act?
quiz.explanation: Indonesia's Job Creation Law (Cipta Kerja) was a sweeping omnibus legislation amending over 70 existing laws simultaneously to deregulate the economy and simplify business licensing.

laws.title: New Capital City Nusantara Law
laws.subtitle: Indonesia's law establishing the new capital Nusantara in Borneo
laws.fullDescription: Indonesia enacted legislation establishing Nusantara as the country's new capital in East Kalimantan, Borneo, replacing Jakarta which faces severe flooding, land subsidence, and overcrowding. The law creates a special governance structure for the new capital territory, sets land use regulations, establishes relocation timelines for government ministries, and provides investment incentives for the development. The project involves carving a city of 1.7 million planned residents from tropical forest. Environmental groups raised concerns about deforestation and displacement of indigenous communities.
laws.penalty: Land speculation in the Nusantara special territory carries criminal penalties; unauthorized clearing of forest in the development zone without permit carries fines and imprisonment; indigenous land rights violations trigger compensation requirements
exceptions: Indigenous communities with recognized customary land rights have protected status
Existing agricultural communities have transition and relocation support
Environmental conservation zones within Nusantara boundaries are legally protected

quiz.q: Why is Indonesia relocating its capital from Jakarta to Nusantara in Borneo?
options: Jakarta was recently damaged by an earthquake
Borneo is more centrally located geographically
Jakarta faces severe flooding, land subsidence, and overcrowding
The government seeks to develop Eastern Indonesia economically
quiz.explanation: Jakarta faces multiple existential threats including severe flooding (partly worsened by land subsidence from excessive groundwater extraction), overcrowding as one of the world's most populous metropolitan areas, and infrastructure that has reached its limits — driving the decision to build a new purpose-built capital.

laws.title: New Criminal Code Morality Provisions
laws.subtitle: Indonesia's controversial new criminal code with morality offenses
laws.fullDescription: Indonesia enacted a new Criminal Code in 2023 replacing its Dutch colonial-era Wetboek van Strafrecht, taking effect in 2026. The new code contains highly controversial provisions including criminalizing extramarital sex (between unmarried cohabitants), potentially restricting contraception promotion, criminalizing insults to the president and state institutions, and creating vague public nuisance offenses. The provisions drew international concern about tourism and foreign investment impacts, and domestic opposition from civil liberties groups. The government emphasized the provisions mainly apply to complainant-driven prosecutions between relatives.
laws.penalty: Extramarital sex carries up to 1 year imprisonment; insulting the president carries up to 3 years; living together without marriage carries up to 6 months; inducing miscarriage carries up to 4 years
exceptions: The extramarital sex provision can only be reported by a spouse or relative, not by police
Tourist areas have modified enforcement approaches
Medical providers performing legal procedures are not subject to the broader morality provisions
laws.sourceLabel: Indonesian Ministry of Law and Human Rights

quiz.q: A key limitation on Indonesia's new extramarital sex criminalization is that it can only be reported by whom?
options: A spouse or relative of the parties involved
quiz.explanation: A key constraint in Indonesia's new Criminal Code is that the extramarital sex provision can only be reported by a spouse or relative of the parties involved — it cannot be initiated by police or any third party, limiting but not eliminating its practical impact as a prosecutorial tool.

laws.title: Indonesia Prabowo Presidential Victory and Dynastic Politics
laws.subtitle: 2024 election win and Jokowi family's continued political influence
laws.fullDescription: Prabowo Subianto won Indonesia's February 2024 presidential election with 58% of the vote, with Gibran Rakabuming Raka (son of outgoing President Joko Widodo) as his running mate. The Constitutional Court had controversially lowered the minimum age for vice-presidential candidates from 40 to permit 36-year-old Gibran's candidacy. Prabowo's Gerindra party formed a broad coalition government. Critics raised concerns about democratic backsliding and nepotism, while supporters emphasized Prabowo's strong anti-corruption and defense credentials.
laws.penalty: Electoral violations under Law No. 7/2017 on General Elections carry fines of Rp 24 million–500 million ($1,500–32,000) and up to 4 years imprisonment for serious offenses.
exceptions: Campaign finance violations by minor parties subject to administrative fines only
International election observers granted immunity from campaign finance reporting requirements

quiz.q: What constitutional change allowed Gibran Rakabuming Raka to run as vice president in Indonesia's 2024 election?
options: The minimum age for VP candidates was lowered from 40
A special 'presidential family' exception was created
The election age was lowered to 17
quiz.explanation: Indonesia's Constitutional Court ruled to lower the minimum age for vice-presidential candidates from 40 years, allowing 36-year-old Gibran Rakabuming Raka — son of President Jokowi — to run as Prabowo's running mate. The ruling was controversial and criticized as enabling dynastic politics.

laws.title: Indonesia Nickel Export Ban and Downstream Processing Mandate
laws.subtitle: Forcing mineral processing onshore to capture more economic value
laws.fullDescription: Indonesia banned raw nickel ore exports in January 2020 and has steadily enforced the ban while expanding the downstream processing requirement to other minerals. The policy forced global stainless steel and battery producers to invest in Indonesian nickel processing facilities, transforming Indonesia into a major player in battery supply chains. Indonesia expanded similar bans to bauxite (2023) and copper concentrates (scheduled). The policy, while successful in attracting investment, was contested at the WTO by the EU.
laws.penalty: Illegal export of raw nickel ore: criminal charges under Indonesia's Mining Law, imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to IDR 100 billion.
exceptions: Low-grade nickel limonite ore below specific quality thresholds subject to different export rules
Temporary exceptions for domestic emergency supply situations authorized by Minister of Energy
Test batches for new processing facilities may be exported under special research licenses

quiz.q: When did Indonesia implement its ban on raw nickel ore exports?
quiz.explanation: Indonesia implemented its ban on raw nickel ore exports in January 2020, forcing global nickel consumers to invest in Indonesian processing facilities. The policy successfully transformed Indonesia into a major downstream nickel processing hub critical to battery supply chains.

laws.title: Indonesia Electronic Information and Transactions Law Reform
laws.subtitle: Narrowing overbroad criminal defamation provisions
laws.fullDescription: Indonesia enacted revisions to its Electronic Information and Transactions (ITE) Law in 2024, narrowing the overbroad 'defamation' and 'unpleasant feelings' provisions that had been used to criminalize legitimate speech, including criticism of officials and online discussions. The original provisions had led to thousands of prosecutions and were internationally criticized. Revisions required specific intent, applied graduated penalties, and added procedural safeguards. Criticism of public officials in matters of public interest received stronger protection.
laws.penalty: Criminal online defamation under revised ITE Law: maximum 2 years imprisonment (reduced from 6 years). Content inciting hatred based on race, religion, or ethnicity: imprisonment up to 6 years.
exceptions: Journalistic reporting by registered media organizations protected as press freedom even if critical of officials
Academic publications and research discussing sensitive social issues protected under freedom of expression provisions
Anonymous reporting of corruption to official anti-corruption channels not subject to ITE criminal liability

quiz.q: What was the original maximum prison sentence for online defamation under Indonesia's original ITE Law?
quiz.explanation: Indonesia's original ITE Law carried a maximum 6-year imprisonment for online defamation — widely criticized as disproportionate and used to silence government critics. The 2024 revision reduced the maximum to 2 years and added safeguards, following international pressure and domestic advocacy.

laws.title: Nickel Export Ban and Battery Industrialisation
laws.subtitle: Indonesia bans raw nickel ore exports to force domestic processing
laws.fullDescription: Indonesia banned the export of unprocessed nickel ore, requiring all nickel to be processed into higher-value products (nickel pig iron, stainless steel, battery precursors) within Indonesia. The policy attracted massive Chinese investment in smelters on Sulawesi and Halmahera. Indonesia is challenging a WTO ruling against the ban while also negotiating exemptions within free trade agreements.
laws.penalty: Companies exporting raw nickel ore: confiscation of shipments and fines up to $1M USD per violation
exceptions: Low-grade limonite ore with nickel content under 1.7% subject to separate rules
Research and testing quantities exempt

quiz.q: What is Indonesia's stated goal for banning raw nickel ore exports?
options: Forcing domestic processing to capture higher value
quiz.explanation: Indonesia's nickel export ban aims to force domestic processing of nickel into higher-value products, keeping more economic value within Indonesia and building a domestic battery industry.

laws.title: Nusantara Capital City Law and Kalimantan Development
laws.subtitle: Indonesia builds new capital city Nusantara on Borneo
laws.fullDescription: Indonesia enacted the Nusantara Capital City Law, establishing the legal framework for the new national capital on the island of Kalimantan (Borneo). The law created the Nusantara Capital Authority with special powers over land use, investment, and governance. The government began relocating civil servants, constructing government buildings, and managing the environmental impact on the rainforest area.
laws.penalty: Illegal land occupation in the Nusantara development zone: eviction and fines; environmental crimes in buffer zone: up to 10 years
exceptions: Indigenous Dayak communities with prior land claims receive consultation and compensation rights
Existing businesses in the area get transition periods before zoning restrictions take effect

quiz.q: On which island is Indonesia's new capital city Nusantara being built?
quiz.explanation: Indonesia's new capital city Nusantara is being built on the island of Kalimantan (Borneo), moving the capital from Jakarta which faces severe land subsidence, flooding, and overpopulation problems.

laws.title: Prabowo Presidency and Defence Modernisation Laws
laws.subtitle: Indonesia's new president prioritises military spending and food security
laws.fullDescription: Prabowo Subianto — a former military commander — won Indonesia's February 2024 presidential election and enacted legislation prioritising defence modernisation (targeting 1.5% GDP military spending), a national food estate programme to achieve food self-sufficiency, and infrastructure expansion in Kalimantan for the Nusantara capital. Critics raised concerns about democratic backsliding given Prabowo's human rights record.
laws.penalty: Defence procurement fraud: criminal prosecution under military justice and civilian anti-corruption frameworks
exceptions: Existing civilian oversight of military maintained under constitutional provisions
International human rights treaty obligations continue regardless of government priorities

quiz.q: What was Prabowo Subianto's previous career before becoming Indonesia's president?
quiz.explanation: Prabowo Subianto is a former military commander who had served as Special Forces (Kopassus) commander — a background that attracted controversy due to alleged human rights violations but also strong nationalist support.

laws.title: Palm Oil Sustainability and EUDR Compliance Law
laws.subtitle: Indonesia aligns palm oil with EU deforestation regulation
laws.fullDescription: Indonesia enacted a Palm Oil Sustainable Certification Law requiring all palm oil exports to the EU to meet the EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR) standards, with satellite traceability from plantation to export. The law created a national palm oil certification authority, mandated smallholder inclusion in certification programmes, and penalised companies that used deforestation-linked supply chains.
laws.penalty: Palm oil exporters using deforested land: export bans to the EU and fines up to $5M; certification fraud: criminal prosecution
exceptions: Smallholder farmers (under 25 hectares) receive 3-year implementation support and subsidised certification
Existing plantations planted before 2020 not subject to deforestation certification requirements

quiz.q: Why is palm oil compliance with the EU Deforestation Regulation critical for Indonesia?
options: Indonesia is trying to export palm oil to China
Indonesia is the world's largest palm oil producer and the EU is a major market
EU wants to buy more Indonesian palm oil
Indonesia depends on EU palm oil imports for food
quiz.explanation: Indonesia is the world's largest palm oil producer, and the European Union is one of its most important export markets — meaning that failure to comply with the EU's anti-deforestation requirements could cost Indonesia billions in palm oil export revenue.

laws.title: Indonesia Critical Minerals Downstream Processing Mandate
laws.subtitle: Nickel and cobalt value chain integration
laws.fullDescription: Indonesia enacted the Critical Minerals Strategic Processing and Export Restriction Act 2025, expanding its controversial nickel ore export ban model to cobalt, bauxite, and copper. The law prohibits raw ore exports for covered minerals, mandates that processing capacity be established within Indonesia before export is permitted (following the nickel model that drove massive Chinese investment in Indonesian smelting), creates the Indonesia Critical Minerals Authority with oversight of joint venture requirements, mandates 51% Indonesian ownership in new processing investments, and establishes a $10 billion Critical Minerals Industrial Fund for infrastructure supporting processing zones. The law drew WTO dispute threats from the EU and Japan.
laws.penalty: Raw ore export without processing exemption: $100 million per shipment plus license revocation; joint venture ownership fraud: 25 years imprisonment; industrial zone environmental violation: IDR 100 billion plus remediation
exceptions: Small-scale mining operations under 1,000 tonnes/month exempt from processing mandate
Samples and scientific specimens exempt from export restrictions
Emergency supply agreements during global disruption reviewed by Ministry
laws.sourceLabel: Indonesia Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources

quiz.q: Indonesia's Critical Minerals Act expands the export ban model from nickel to which other minerals?
quiz.explanation: Indonesia's Critical Minerals Strategic Processing Act extends its proven nickel ore export ban model to cobalt, bauxite, and copper — forcing downstream processing investment to occur within Indonesia rather than in consuming countries.

laws.title: Indonesia Prabowo Administration New Capital and Development Act
laws.subtitle: Nusantara capital city and national development agenda
laws.fullDescription: Indonesia enacted the National Development Acceleration and New Capital Nusantara Implementation Act 2025 under President Prabowo Subianto, continuing the Jokowi-era Nusantara new capital city project in East Kalimantan. The law accelerates the Nusantara development timeline with mandatory government ministry relocation by 2028, establishes the Nusantara Capital Authority with streamlined permitting and investment attraction powers, creates tax-free special zones for high-tech and financial services in Nusantara, introduces the Prabowo Food Estate Programme expanding agricultural production in Kalimantan and Papua for food self-sufficiency, and establishes the National Connectivity Programme building 15,000km of toll roads and upgrading 100 airports and ports by 2030.
laws.penalty: Nusantara construction unauthorized development: IDR 10 billion plus demolition; Food Estate Programme procurement fraud: 25 years imprisonment; connectivity programme contractor fraud: IDR 50 billion
exceptions: Indigenous Dayak communities in Nusantara zone retain recognized land rights with compensation negotiation
Environmental protected areas in East Kalimantan explicitly excluded from Nusantara development zone
Emergency infrastructure works at existing Jakarta government buildings continue during transition

quiz.q: In which Indonesian province is the new capital city Nusantara being constructed?
quiz.explanation: Indonesia's new capital city Nusantara is being constructed in East Kalimantan, on the island of Borneo — chosen for its central geographic location within the Indonesian archipelago and to reduce the extreme overcrowding and flooding burden on Jakarta.

laws.title: Prabowo Administration Defense and Food Security Act
laws.subtitle: New president's military expansion and agricultural self-sufficiency
laws.fullDescription: President Prabowo Subianto's administration has enacted sweeping legislation combining defense modernization with a national food security initiative. The law allocates a major defense budget increase for domestic weapons production, restructures the military's territorial command system, and launches a 'Food Estate' program converting forests and peatlands to agricultural use. Critics raise concerns about environmental damage and human rights implications.
laws.penalty: Unauthorized occupation of designated Food Estate lands carries fines and imprisonment up to three years. Companies that fail defense production offset requirements face contract cancellation.
exceptions: Indigenous communities with recognized land rights are entitled to consultation and compensation before Food Estate conversion
Small-scale farmers who voluntarily participate in the program receive subsidized inputs and guaranteed purchase prices

quiz.q: What is the controversial environmental aspect of Indonesia's Food Estate program?
options: Converting forests and peatlands to agriculture
quiz.explanation: The Food Estate program's conversion of forests and peatlands to agricultural land has drawn criticism for potential deforestation and greenhouse gas emissions.

laws.title: Nusantara New Capital City Development Act
laws.subtitle: Building the new capital in Borneo
laws.fullDescription: Indonesia enacted updated Nusantara new capital legislation accelerating development of the new capital city being built in East Kalimantan (Borneo), replacing Jakarta. The law provides new incentives for private investment in the capital's development, resolves land rights disputes with local indigenous Dayak communities, establishes the governance structure for the new capital territory, and sets mandatory timelines for government relocation from Jakarta.
laws.penalty: Developers who violate land rights agreements with indigenous communities face project suspension and compensation orders. Fraudulent land acquisition in the capital territory carries up to 10 years imprisonment.
exceptions: The President's office and key ministries receive priority relocation funding while smaller agencies have extended timelines
Existing businesses in Jakarta retain their legal status without any obligation to relocate

quiz.q: On which island of Indonesia is the new capital Nusantara being built?
quiz.explanation: Nusantara is being built in East Kalimantan province on the island of Borneo, chosen partly for its central location and lower earthquake risk compared to Jakarta, and partly to reduce the burden on overpopulated Java.

laws.title: Nickel Downstream Processing and EV Battery Industry Act
laws.subtitle: Transforming raw material exports into industrial products
laws.fullDescription: Indonesia enacted legislation expanding its successful nickel export ban policy to other strategic minerals, requiring domestic processing before export. Building on its nickel export ban that forced global battery companies to invest in Indonesia, the law extends the downstream processing requirement to bauxite and copper, creates incentives for battery gigafactory construction, and establishes a critical minerals diplomacy framework with EV-producing nations.
laws.penalty: Export of unprocessed restricted minerals carries fines up to IDR 1 billion per shipment and license revocation. Companies that receive investment incentives for processing facilities but export raw materials face subsidy recovery and criminal liability.
exceptions: Small-scale miners operating traditional methods have a five-year grace period before downstream requirements apply to them
Emergency exemptions may be granted for specific trade partner relationships during supply chain disruptions

quiz.q: What critical battery mineral did Indonesia ban raw exports of, forcing global companies to invest in Indonesian processing?
quiz.explanation: Indonesia — the world's largest nickel producer — banned the export of unprocessed nickel ore in 2020, forcing EV battery companies to build processing facilities in Indonesia if they wanted Indonesian nickel. The strategy successfully attracted billions in foreign investment.

laws.title: Deforestation-Free Supply Chain and Palm Oil Sustainability Act
laws.subtitle: Addressing EU deforestation regulation compliance
laws.fullDescription: Indonesia enacted legislation responding to the EU's Deforestation Regulation requiring companies to prove their products don't come from deforested land. The law creates a traceability system for palm oil, coffee, and cocoa, establishes satellite monitoring of plantations, creates certification standards compatible with EU requirements, and provides transition support for smallholder farmers who need to prove their land compliance.
laws.penalty: Companies that falsify deforestation-free certification face up to 10 years imprisonment and export license revocation. Plantation owners who clear forests after the certification cutoff face fines up to IDR 15 billion per hectare.
exceptions: Smallholder farmers with plots under 25 hectares receive simplified certification pathways
Traditional subsistence forest use by indigenous communities is exempt from the plantation certification requirements

quiz.q: What major EU regulation did Indonesia's sustainability law need to comply with?
options: EU Deforestation Regulation requiring proof products don't come from deforested land
quiz.explanation: The EU Deforestation Regulation (effective 2023) requires companies selling products like palm oil, soy, coffee, cocoa, cattle, wood, and rubber in the EU to prove they didn't contribute to deforestation after December 31, 2020. This creates major compliance requirements for Indonesian exporters.

laws.title: Indonesia Prabowo Defense-Forward Foreign Policy and Military Act
laws.subtitle: ASEAN Leadership and Strategic Autonomy Law
laws.fullDescription: Establishes Indonesia's foreign policy posture under President Prabowo Subianto emphasizing strategic autonomy, ASEAN centrality, and military modernization. The law increases defense spending to 1.5% of GDP, creates the Indonesian Defense Industrial Framework for domestic weapons production, establishes bilateral defense agreements with major powers while maintaining non-alignment, and mandates a 1 million-strong reserve force expansion.
laws.penalty: Criminal prosecution for defense procurement corruption; fines for contractors violating technology transfer requirements
exceptions: Strategic intelligence partnerships maintained under classified frameworks
Emergency procurement may bypass standard competitive bidding

quiz.q: What foreign policy principle does Indonesia's Prabowo Defense Act emphasize?
quiz.explanation: Indonesia's foreign policy under President Prabowo emphasizes strategic autonomy and ASEAN centrality, maintaining non-alignment.

laws.title: Indonesia Nickel Downstream Processing and EV Battery Hub Act
laws.subtitle: Critical Mineral Value Chain Development Law
laws.fullDescription: Expands Indonesia's ban on raw nickel ore exports to force value-added processing domestically. The law mandates nickel processing into nickel pig iron, ferronickel, and battery-grade nickel sulfate within Indonesia, creates the Indonesia Battery Corporation as a state enterprise, establishes partnerships with Korean, Chinese, and US EV manufacturers for battery gigafactories, and protects marine ecosystems from nickel mining in Sulawesi.
laws.penalty: Export license revocation for companies exporting unprocessed nickel; fines up to IDR 100 billion
exceptions: Low-grade nickel ore below specified thresholds may be exported during transition
Emergency supply agreements with processing plants under construction
laws.sourceLabel: Indonesia Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources

quiz.q: What does Indonesia's Nickel Processing Act ban the export of?
quiz.explanation: Indonesia bans the export of raw nickel ore to force domestic processing into higher-value products like battery-grade nickel sulfate.

laws.title: Indonesia Prabowo Nusantara Capital Continuation and Development Act
laws.subtitle: New Capital City Construction and Development Law
laws.fullDescription: Continues the construction of Nusantara as Indonesia's new capital city in East Kalimantan, now under President Prabowo following the transition from Jokowi. The law maintains the Nusantara Capital Authority, continues government agency relocation timelines, creates infrastructure development frameworks, establishes environmental mitigation requirements for Borneo forest impacts, and creates the Nusantara smart city governance framework.
laws.penalty: Contractor fines for construction delays; environmental liability for Borneo ecosystem damage
exceptions: Presidential and government core functions relocate first before full civil service transfer
Environmental sensitive areas have modified construction protocols

quiz.q: In which Indonesian island is the new capital Nusantara being built?
quiz.explanation: Indonesia's new capital Nusantara is being built in East Kalimantan on the island of Borneo (Kalimantan), away from overcrowded Java.

laws.title: Prabowo Subianto Presidency and Jokowi Legacy
laws.subtitle: Former General Wins After Two Previous Defeats
laws.fullDescription: Prabowo Subianto won Indonesia's February 2024 presidential election decisively, succeeding Joko Widodo after two previous defeats in 2014 and 2019. Prabowo, a former special forces general with a controversial human rights record, had been rehabilitated politically through Jokowi's cabinet. His running mate was Jokowi's son Gibran Rakabuming Raka.
laws.penalty: No criminal penalties; democratic election outcome
exceptions: Constitutional term limit for Jokowi
Running mate age eligibility controversy

quiz.q: How many times had Prabowo run for Indonesia's presidency before winning in 2024?
quiz.explanation: Prabowo ran for president twice before winning in 2024 — he lost to Joko Widodo in both 2014 and 2019 before prevailing on his third attempt.

laws.title: Critical Minerals Downstream Processing Policy
laws.subtitle: Indonesia Bans Raw Nickel Export to Force Value Addition
laws.fullDescription: Indonesia maintained its ban on raw nickel ore exports, enforced since 2020, requiring domestic processing before export. The policy successfully attracted major investments in nickel processing and electric vehicle battery manufacturing. Indonesia emerged as a critical player in the global EV battery supply chain.
laws.penalty: Criminal penalties for illegal raw ore exports; customs violations
exceptions: Government-approved processing facility certifications
Special economic zone provisions

quiz.q: Why did Indonesia ban raw nickel ore exports?
options: To force domestic value-added processing and attract investment
quiz.explanation: Indonesia banned raw nickel exports to force downstream processing domestically, successfully attracting major investments in nickel processing and EV battery manufacturing.

laws.title: Nusantara New Capital City Construction
laws.subtitle: Indonesia Relocates Capital From Jakarta
