The cause was a combination of aging oil fields in Sumatra and Kalimantan producing less, while Indonesia's rapidly growing economy and population drove domestic consumption higher. New exploration could not replace declining legacy production fast enough. This energy transition has significant fiscal implications: Indonesia's fuel subsidies are enormous and create both budgetary and environmental challenges.

laws.title: Undang-Undang Perkawinan — Marriage Law
laws.subtitle: Marriage law in Indonesia's religiously diverse society
laws.fullDescription: Indonesia's Marriage Law (1974) requires that marriages conform to the bride's and groom's respective religions — effectively making interfaith marriage legally impossible without one party converting. Muslims follow Islamic Marriage Law (KHI) administered through religious courts. Same-sex marriage is not recognized; homosexuality, while not explicitly criminalized at federal level, is targeted by the new Penal Code morality provisions and local Sharia regulations in Aceh. Minimum marriage age raised to 19 for both parties (2019, previously 16 for women). Child marriage remains common in rural areas despite the legal age. Indonesia has among Asia's highest rates of underage marriage.
laws.penalty: Marriage without government registration: civil penalties, no legal recognition. Child marriage under 19 facilitated by parents or guardians: civil liability. Marriage registration fraud: criminal prosecution.
exceptions: Customary (adat) marriages may receive recognition if registered within a year
Religious courts handle Muslim family disputes; civil courts handle non-Muslim and interfaith matters
Foreign nationals may marry under their own national law with bilateral recognition
laws.sourceLabel: Kementerian Hukum dan HAM — Ministry of Law and Human Rights

quiz.q: What makes interfaith marriage legally impossible in Indonesia under the 1974 Marriage Law?
options: The government must approve all marriages regardless of religion — approvals are denied across religions
Marriages must conform to the religion of both parties — since different religious laws govern differently, interfaith couples cannot legally marry without conversion
All Indonesians must marry under Islamic law regardless of their personal religion
Marriages are only legal if performed by a government officer, not religious officiants
quiz.explanation: Indonesia's 1974 Marriage Law requires marriages to be performed according to each party's religion. Since Indonesian law recognizes 6 official religions with separate marriage laws (Islamic, Protestant, Catholic, Hindu, Buddhist, Confucian), a Muslim cannot legally marry a Christian without one converting — because no religious law governs an interfaith union. This effectively makes interfaith marriage impossible without religious conversion, despite Indonesia's secular constitutional framework.

laws.title: Undang-Undang Terorisme — Counter-Terrorism Law
laws.subtitle: Indonesia's response to Jemaah Islamiyah and post-Bali bombing
laws.fullDescription: Indonesia's Counter-Terrorism Law (2002, strengthened 2018) was passed after the 2002 Bali bombing killed 202 people (88 Australians, 38 Indonesians, many others) — Indonesia's worst terrorist attack. Jemaah Islamiyah (JI) was a regional terrorist network with Al-Qaeda links responsible for the Bali bombings and other attacks. The National Counter-Terrorism Agency (BNPT) and Detachment 88 (counterterrorism police) have been internationally praised for dismantling JI. The 2018 amendments: extended pre-charge detention to 21 days (extendable to 28), criminalized travel to terrorist-training destinations, and created deradicalization programs. The BNPT runs prison-based deradicalization programs.
laws.penalty: Planning or executing terrorist act: death penalty or life imprisonment. Joining terrorist organization: up to 15 years. Financing terrorism: up to 15 years.
exceptions: Former terrorists who cooperate with authorities and complete deradicalization may receive sentence reductions
Individuals who voluntarily surrender and provide intelligence receive statutory leniency
Journalists covering terrorist groups for journalistic purposes not criminalized
laws.sourceLabel: Badan Nasional Penanggulangan Terorisme — National Counter-Terrorism Agency

quiz.q: What event triggered Indonesia's Counter-Terrorism Law in 2002?
options: A series of church bombings by Christian-Muslim sectarian conflict
The 2002 Bali bombing by Jemaah Islamiyah killing 202 people including 88 Australians
An assassination attempt on President Megawati
The September 11 attacks prompting Indonesian preventive legislation
quiz.explanation: The October 2002 Bali bombing — car bombs detonated in Kuta's nightclub district — killed 202 people (the deadliest terrorist attack in Indonesian history) and shocked Australia, which lost 88 citizens. Jemaah Islamiyah, the perpetrator, was a regional Islamist network with Al-Qaeda connections spanning Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, and the Philippines. Indonesia rapidly enacted counter-terrorism legislation and built Detachment 88 — which has been internationally recognized for successfully dismantling JI's operational network.
